title: Near-patient diagnosis of the cause and treatability of most serious infections

concept.text: The proposed innovation is an affordable diagnostic capability available close to where a patient receives care that answers three connected questions: what is causing a serious infection, whether a detected organism actually explains the illness, and which available treatments are likely to work. It would deliver results quickly enough to guide initial treatment across diverse infection syndromes and specimen types, including mixed infections and organisms that were not anticipated when the test was designed. This is a proposed capability, not an achievement established by the supplied evidence.

Conceptual synthesis: the advance requires an integrated chain of detection, causal interpretation and actionable susceptibility assessment, with uncertainty communicated at each stage. Detecting microbial genetic material would not by itself establish the cause of illness or determine effective treatment. A faster assay restricted to a fixed list of organisms could contribute to this capability, but would cover only part of its intended breadth. “Most serious infections” describes an ambition whose clinical coverage still needs an operational definition.

significance.text: Conditional significance: if the proposed accuracy, speed, affordability and breadth were demonstrated, clinicians could make informed treatment decisions at the first encounter across many serious infections. The direct advance would be timely, actionable diagnostic information. Reduced reliance on empiric treatment would be a potential consequence whose extent depends on specimen availability, diagnostic reliability and whether results arrive before treatment decisions must be made.

Further potential benefits include more appropriate use of existing antimicrobials and earlier recognition of infections outside familiar diagnostic panels. These possibilities require clinical demonstration. Identifying an unfamiliar organism is useful only when there is enough evidence to interpret its relevance to the patient, and a susceptibility result helps only when it can inform an available treatment. Faster laboratory information alone does not establish improved patient outcomes.

An important limit is that this would improve diagnosis and treatment selection; it would not itself create a drug for an untreatable infection, prevent transmission or replace vaccination. Its revolutionary scope therefore rests on combining breadth, accessibility and clinical interpretation, rather than speed alone. These are implications of the proposed concept, not measured effects established by the supplied sources.

missing_breakthrough.text: Conceptual barrier: a broadly useful near-patient system must obtain a clinically meaningful answer from specimens that may contain very little relevant microbial material—or none from the actual site of infection. Greater analytical sensitivity cannot recover a pathogen that is absent from the collected specimen. The proposed capability therefore requires suitable sampling strategies and explicit recognition of when a negative result cannot safely exclude infection. The supplied scientific artifacts do not independently substantiate the frequency or magnitude of these limitations.

Conceptual barrier: detection must be connected to causation. Contamination, harmless colonization and multiple detected organisms can complicate attribution of illness. The system would need to distinguish plausible causes from incidental findings, recognize mixed infections and communicate unresolved alternatives. For previously unrecognized organisms, discovering a sequence and establishing clinical relevance are separate tasks.

Conceptual barrier: pathogen identification must also be connected to treatment response. The research raises the limitation that a genome alone may not reliably predict drug response; the supplied evidence does not establish when or how often this occurs. The missing capability is therefore actionable susceptibility assessment with a defined scope and uncertainty, rather than an assumption that identifying genetic material completes the treatment decision.

Engineering synthesis: these functions must work together within the time, cost, staffing and infrastructure constraints of hospitals and resource-limited clinics. A convincing system must preserve diagnostic and susceptibility performance while moving testing close to care. A successful individual component would be partial progress; the proposed innovation requires the combined workflow to remain clinically useful.

current_state.text: The research identifies clinical metagenomic sequencing as an existing approach to broad organism detection and names a study attributed to Benoit and colleagues, “Seven-year performance of a clinical metagenomic next-generation sequencing test for diagnosis of central nervous system infections,” with a reported publication date of 12 November 2024. It reports 63.1% sensitivity in an evaluated subset and missed infections where microbial material was absent from cerebrospinal fluid. Those details remain unverified in the supplied review: the retained PubMed material contains a cookie-access message rather than article content, and the earlier inspection on which the research relies was not supplied. The denominator, reference standard and precise meaning of the reported sensitivity therefore cannot be established here, and the number should not be generalized to other specimens or serious infections.

The research also names a study attributed to Banerjee and colleagues, “Fast Antimicrobial Susceptibility Testing for Gram-Negative Bacteremia: The FAST Randomized Clinical Trial,” with a reported publication date of 18 April 2026. It describes rapid testing as failing to show superiority on the overall trial outcome. No article text was retained for the supplied JAMA link, so the study identity, date, endpoint and result cannot be independently confirmed from these inputs. The reported conclusion must remain an unverified account; it cannot establish either clinical benefit or absence of benefit. The broader distinction remains useful: faster susceptibility results and improved clinical outcomes are separate propositions.

Evidence boundary: the supplied materials do not establish a demonstrated system that combines broad detection, causal interpretation, actionable susceptibility and near-patient accessibility across most serious infections. They also do not provide a substantive search record supporting an assessment of developments through 1 November 2026. This limits what can be concluded about current achievements and whether the full capability remains unsolved; it is not evidence that the referenced studies are false or that no further progress exists.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: prospective studies should evaluate the integrated workflow in hospitals and resource-limited clinics across prespecified serious-infection syndromes, patient populations and specimen types. Coverage should include mixed infections and organisms outside the system’s anticipated targets, with clear definitions of what counts as previously unrecognized. The studies should define the clinical denominator behind “most serious infections.” Finite evaluations would establish demonstrated breadth within their tested settings, not literal universality.
completion_criteria.label: Prospective integrated workflow studies establish breadth across serious infections

completion_criteria.text: Proposed measurement framework: before evaluation, investigators should specify acceptable turnaround time from sampling to an actionable result, affordability, diagnostic accuracy, causal-attribution performance and susceptibility performance. They should separately assess pathogen detection, interpretation of clinical relevance and treatment guidance. Uncertainty reporting should be evaluated explicitly, including how the system handles inadequate specimens, ambiguous detections, incomplete susceptibility coverage and negative results that cannot exclude infection. These are proposed criteria, not established standards, and no numerical thresholds are supplied.
completion_criteria.label: Prespecified diagnostic performance criteria include explicit uncertainty assessment

completion_criteria.text: Proposed clinical demonstration: randomized implementation studies should show improved patient outcomes or more appropriate treatment, using clearly defined endpoints and prespecified acceptable rates of dangerous false reassurance and false attribution. Evaluation should establish whether results arrive in time to change decisions, whether clinicians act on them appropriately and whether recommended treatments are available. Faster analytical results alone would not satisfy the clinical-benefit claim.
completion_criteria.label: Randomized implementation studies demonstrate clinical benefit within prespecified safety limits

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries: independent sites should reproduce performance across operators, routine specimen handling and the infrastructure conditions of intended use. Reports should identify excluded syndromes and specimens, failure rates, costs and circumstances requiring additional testing or specialist interpretation. Demonstrated success could support a bounded clinical claim while preserving explicit limitations outside the evaluated scope.
completion_criteria.label: Independent sites reproduce routine performance and report practical limitations

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: INF-06, a dependable platform for generating new antibacterial treatments, and INF-15, a rapidly adaptable clinical phage-therapy platform, overlap most directly through treatment selection. INF-05 could help identify relevant infections and assess susceptibility, while those concepts concern producing or adapting therapies. INF-07, broad-spectrum treatment for unrelated viral infections, could reduce some dependence on identifying a specific virus before treatment, but would not answer all questions of causation, coverage or treatability.

Roster-based synthesis: INF-02, a safe, scalable cure for established HIV infection; INF-11, a safe, broadly effective treatment-free cure for chronic hepatitis B; and INF-12, very short, reliable curative treatment for active and latent tuberculosis, concern achieving durable therapeutic outcomes. INF-05 could support diagnosis or treatment decisions where applicable, but identifying an infection and its likely drug response does not establish a cure or demonstrate eradication of persistent infection.

Roster-based synthesis: INF-01, a broadly protective HIV vaccine; INF-03, a tuberculosis vaccine that interrupts transmission; INF-08, a pre-emptive vaccine against diverse pandemic coronaviruses; and INF-13, a highly protective, durable and readily deliverable malaria vaccine, concern prevention. INF-04, a reliable way to break malaria transmission through its vectors, concerns interruption of transmission. INF-05 addresses diagnosis during clinical care and could complement these approaches, while remaining a distinct capability.

Roster-based synthesis: INF-09, a rapid, end-to-end vaccine response to a newly identified pathogen, shares the need to recognize unfamiliar infectious threats. Near-patient detection could potentially contribute early clinical information, but vaccine development and deployment require a separate response capability. INF-10, prevention of multiple sclerosis by controlling Epstein–Barr virus, and INF-14, mechanism-guided prevention of major post-viral syndromes, share questions about linking infection to disease. Detecting an organism during an acute illness would not by itself establish its causal role in a later condition or demonstrate that controlling it prevents that condition.

unresolved_issues: The underlying scientific basis for the stated diagnostic barriers is not independently documented by substantive source content in the supplied materials.
The reported metagenomic study identity, publication date, 63.1% sensitivity, evaluated subset, reference standard and sampling-related missed infections require confirmation from article content.
The FAST trial identity, publication date, primary endpoint, effect estimates and reported lack of superiority remain unverified.
The supplied search record cannot establish developments through 1 November 2026 or resolve whether the full proposed capability remains open.
“Near-patient,” “rapid,” “affordable,” “most serious infections” and acceptable error rates need operational definitions; the inputs supply no numerical thresholds.
The intended treatment classes and scope of actionable susceptibility assessment remain unspecified.
No substantive review recommendation was rejected; recommendations requiring scientific verification remain unresolved because new research was excluded.

brief.title: Finding infection causes and effective treatments nearby
possible: At a hospital or local clinic, someone with a serious infection could get an affordable answer in time to guide their first treatment: what is causing the illness and which available medicines are likely to work.

The same service could handle many kinds of serious infection, including infections caused by several organisms together or by organisms the test’s designers did not anticipate. It could distinguish a cause of illness from a harmless organism found in the sample.
why: Clinicians could choose treatment with less guesswork at the first encounter. Patients could receive more appropriate medicines, and unfamiliar infections could be recognized earlier.

sources.who: Patrick Benoit and colleagues, University of California, San Francisco
sources.showed: A laboratory test that reads genetic material from many kinds of microbes identified infections of the brain and spinal cord. It found some infections that other tests missed.
sources.quote: When only considering diagnoses made by CSF direct detection testing, the sensitivity of mNGS testing increased to 86%.
sources.cited_for: Broad testing of fluid surrounding the brain and spinal cord can find causes missed by other diagnostic tests.
sources.not_established: The study did not establish a nearby, affordable service that also selects effective treatments across most serious infections.

sources.showed: This is a randomized clinical trial of rapid testing to determine which medicines work against certain bacteria causing bloodstream infections.
sources.cited_for: The trial addresses whether faster drug-response testing improves clinical care.
sources.not_established: Faster drug-response results alone do not establish better patient outcomes.

shown: Benoit and colleagues evaluated broad genetic testing for infections of the brain and spinal cord. In the clinically assessed subset, it detected 63.1% of infections. Some diagnoses came from this test alone, but results typically took days.
missing: Sampling must yield useful answers even when little microbial material is present, while identifying negative results that cannot rule out infection.
A combined test must distinguish illness-causing organisms from contamination or harmless organisms, including when several organisms appear.
Organism detection must connect reliably to which available medicines will work, with clear limits on treatment guidance.
The complete service must work quickly and affordably near patients across diverse serious infections, including in clinics with limited resources.

milestones.label: Broad coverage demonstrated in real patient care
milestones.explanation: Studies following patients through care would have to demonstrate the complete service across defined illnesses, samples and settings, including mixed and unexpected infections. This would establish its clinical reach.

milestones.label: Performance and uncertainty meet criteria set before testing
milestones.explanation: Evaluation would have to assess speed, cost, detection, cause identification, treatment guidance and uncertainty against criteria set beforehand. This would establish when clinicians can rely on the answers.

milestones.label: Randomized studies demonstrate clinical benefit within safety limits
milestones.explanation: Studies randomly assigning use of the service would have to show better outcomes or treatment within preset limits on dangerous errors. This would establish whether timely results improve care.

milestones.label: Independent sites reproduce results in routine use
milestones.explanation: Independent sites would have to reproduce performance under everyday conditions and report failures, costs and situations needing further testing. This would establish practical reliability and limits.

uncertain: What share of serious infections would count as sufficient coverage, and what speed, cost and error rates would be acceptable?
Which treatments could the service assess reliably, especially when an organism’s genetic material does not settle how it responds to drugs?

page.title: Near-patient pathogen identification and susceptibility testing
page.definition: A service at the site of care identifies organisms causing serious infection, distinguishes causative infection from incidental microbial detection, and tests antimicrobial susceptibility—the organism’s response to available drugs. It works across infection syndromes, including mixed infections and organisms outside preset test panels.

goal.need: The UCSF study found central nervous system infections that other tests missed, while missing other infections itself. Speed also requires clinical validation: in FAST, antibiotic escalation or de-escalation occurred a median 14 hours sooner, but the primary patient-outcome test did not establish superiority.

completion.title: Independent clinical evaluation reproduces an integrated near-patient diagnostic service’s claims.
completion.criterion: Independent prospective evaluations reproduce an integrated near-patient service’s registered clinical claims: causal pathogen attribution, actionable susceptibility, results before the treatment decision, and operation within intended-site cost and infrastructure limits. Claims are validated against clinical adjudication and reference susceptibility methods, with patient benefit established in randomised comparisons. Validation spans prespecified serious-infection syndromes and includes mixed infections and organisms outside preset panels; coverage uses all eligible patients as its denominator.
completion.set_by: Technology Atlas; proposed integrated clinical-demonstration test.
completion.basis: Searches of WHO diagnostic priorities, ICMR sepsis product profiles, NIH/BARDA prize criteria and DARPA’s DIGET goals found no joint threshold for coverage, causation, susceptibility, turnaround and cost. The Atlas proposes independent reproduction of an integrated clinical demonstration. No published denominator or numerical coverage threshold supports certifying “most serious infections”; achievement therefore applies only to the validated clinical scope.

milestones.title: An antimicrobial susceptibility assay achieves ≥90% agreement with reference testing.
milestones.criterion: In FDA’s K230675 comparison, essential and categorical agreement must each be ≥90%, false resistance ≤3% of reference-susceptible results and false susceptibility ≤2% of reference-resistant results, with the decision’s error adjustments and exceptions. Essential agreement means minimum inhibitory concentrations within one twofold dilution; categorical agreement means matching susceptibility categories. For amikacin against Pseudomonas aeruginosa, VITEK REVEAL achieved 95.4% for both agreements in 65 specimens, with no major or very major errors.
milestones.set_by: US FDA; K230675 decision summary, page 26. Written for gram-negative positive blood cultures.
milestones.threshold_quote: Performance was considered acceptable if the EA and CA were ≥90%, major error rate was ≤3%, and very major error rate was ≤2%.

milestones.title: A bacterial pathogen assay identifies 90% of isolates to species and 95% to genus.
milestones.criterion: For the bacterial-identification component, meet ICMR TPP.S.II’s minimal targets: 85–90% diagnostic sensitivity, with 90% of isolates identified to species and 95% to genus. The published sepsis conditions specify 1 mL venous blood and blood culture as reference; the panel covers Streptococcus pneumoniae, Streptococcus spp., Staphylococcus aureus, Enterococcus spp., Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Acinetobacter baumannii, Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Salmonella. The figure records related CNS evidence, not validation against these sepsis conditions.
milestones.set_by: ICMR task force and Technical Advisory Group on AMR Diagnostics; Supplementary Table II, TPP.S.II, minimal targets for sepsis. Thresholds appear only in the table.

milestones.title: An antimicrobial susceptibility assay receives FDA 510(k) clearance for its labelled use.
milestones.criterion: FDA issues a substantial-equivalence decision authorising the assay’s labelled clinical use. VITEK REVEAL GN AST Assay and AST System received this decision on 20 June 2024, under K230675. Its indication is susceptibility testing from positive blood cultures containing gram-negative bacilli; separate organism identification is required, and polymicrobial specimens require supplemental testing.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration; K230675, 510(k) Premarket Notification database. The clearance decision appears in the database table.

milestones.title: Near-patient tests identify pathogens within 4 hours and return susceptibility results in under 4 hours.
milestones.criterion: Achieve ICMR TPP.S.II/III’s optimal turnaround, handling, reproducibility and price targets at district or sub-district hospitals: identification ≤4 h; susceptibility profiling <4 h; each with ≤500 µL input, <10 min hands-on time and κ≥0.9 inter-user/site reproducibility. Individual-test prices are ≤INR 500 and ≤INR 2000, respectively. Related urine evidence, published on 3 December 2025, used 53 samples from a 78-patient complicated-UTI cohort: sequencing gave 589/653 susceptibility predictions concordant with VITEK-2 in approximately 4 h from laboratory receipt. This was not a sepsis deployment test.
milestones.set_by: ICMR task force and Technical Advisory Group on AMR Diagnostics; Supplementary Table II, TPP.S.II/III, optimal operational targets for sepsis. Thresholds appear only in the tables.

milestones.title: Rapid susceptibility testing improves 30-day outcomes with a DOOR probability lower 95% bound above 50%.
milestones.criterion: Meet FAST’s superiority test in hospitalised patients with gram-negative bloodstream infection: the lower 95% confidence limit for the probability of a better 30-day Desirability of Outcome Ranking (DOOR), counting ties as one-half, exceeds 50%. DOOR ranks survival without deleterious events, survival with such events, then death. Published on 18 April 2026, FAST analysed 850 of 899 randomised patients at 7 hospitals in 4 countries; its estimate was 48.8% (95% CI 45.3–52.4%), so the threshold was not met.
milestones.set_by: Antibacterial Resistance Leadership Group; FAST protocol NCT06174649 and its published superiority criterion. This test was written for gram-negative bloodstream infection.
milestones.threshold_quote: Superiority was concluded if the lower limit of the 95% CI exceeded 50%.

milestones.title: An integrated near-patient service meets registered diagnostic and treatment endpoints in clinical use.
milestones.criterion: A first prospective clinical evaluation demonstrates the integrated capability defined in the completion criterion, meeting diagnostic, treatment-selection and patient-outcome endpoints registered before enrolment. It evaluates the complete workflow at intended care sites, including clinical attribution of detected organisms, mixed infections and organisms outside preset panels. This first demonstration precedes independent reproduction; the cited studies evaluate components or narrower clinical claims.
milestones.set_by: Technology Atlas; proposed integration milestone. Searches of WHO, ICMR, NIH/BARDA and DARPA documents found component targets, but no published test for this complete workflow.

not_found: Searches of WHO, ICMR, NIH/BARDA and DARPA documents found no external definition of the proportion or denominator meant by “most serious infections”.
No joint published acceptance test for causal attribution, susceptibility, speed, affordability and breadth across serious infections was located.
The full WHO 2020 antibacterial-resistance diagnostic product-profile document could not be opened.
No demonstration meeting the complete integrated capability, including mixed infections and organisms outside preset panels, was located.
No study reporting all the cited ICMR sepsis performance and deployment targets together was located.

results.finding: CSF mNGS detected 26 of 55 bacterial CNS infections, a sensitivity of 47.3%.
results.detail: This is CNS evidence, not validation under the specified sepsis conditions. The study does not report the required proportions of isolates identified to species and genus.

results.finding: For 1,130 UCSF CSF samples, median mNGS laboratory turnaround was 3.6 days.
results.detail: The laboratory turnaround exceeded the four-hour identification target. The study evaluated a centralized identification assay, not the complete near-patient identification and susceptibility workflow.
results.quote:
The median turnaround times for UCSF and non-UCSF patients were 8.2 and 11.4 days, respectively, from sample collection to result (P
< 0.0001), and 3.6 and 3.8 days, respectively, from start of sample processing in the laboratory to result (P
< 0.0001).

results.finding: VITEK REVEAL amikacin testing: 100% essential agreement in 30 results from contrived positive blood cultures.
results.detail: The sample-stability study used 25 isolates overall, with replicate testing. The 30 results were compared with the modal broth microdilution MIC; the table does not report categorical agreement or major and very major error rates for this comparison.

results.finding: PhenEXA AST achieved 100% essential agreement with broth microdilution across 12 bacterial strains tested with two antibiotics each.
results.detail: Categorical agreement was also 100%. The excerpt does not report the reference-susceptible and reference-resistant denominators or the error adjustments and exceptions needed to assess the full criterion.
results.quote: When comparing the results of MA-MIC and GMM-MIC with the conventional BMD method, PhenEXA demonstrated strong agreement, achieving 100% EA (defined as MIC within one log2 dilution of that obtained using the standard BMD method) and CA (defined as agreement in bacteria-drug susceptibility profile based on CLSI MIC breakpoints).

results.finding: T2Bacteria identified proven bloodstream infections in 35 of 39 patients with targeted-organism-positive blood cultures: 90% sensitivity.
results.detail: Testing used at least 3 mL of blood and targeted five species, leaving several organisms in the specified panel uncovered. The study did not establish the required species- and genus-level identification rates across the specified panel.
results.quote:
Sensitivity of T2Bacteria for proven BSI was 90%
(95% CI, 76% to 96%) ( Table 2 ).

results.finding: FilmArray ME identified S. pneumoniae in 4 culture-positive CSF specimens, with 100% sensitivity.
results.detail: The study tested 1,560 CSF specimens against CSF culture. It did not report overall species- or genus-level identification rates, and its fixed panel did not cover all cultured bacteria. It was not validated under the specified sepsis conditions.

results.finding: In 53 complicated UTI samples, the optimized assay achieved 99% pathogen-identification accuracy (100/101).
results.detail: The score includes 13 correctly identified negative samples; it does not establish the required species- and genus-level percentages or diagnostic sensitivity. Testing used urine and routine culture-based identification, not the specified sepsis conditions.
results.quote:
The optimized method (M + BB + NB, method 11) demonstrated an overall accuracy score of 99% (100/101) across 53 samples (Table
1
, Fig.
2
a, c), constituting 88 pathogens correctly identified and 13 negative samples correctly identified.

results.finding: VITEK REVEAL GN AST Assay and AST System received FDA 510(k) clearance on 20 June 2024; sample size not applicable.
results.detail: The labelled use is susceptibility testing from positive blood cultures containing gram-negative bacilli. Organism identification is required, and polymicrobial samples require supplemental susceptibility testing.
results.quote: and have determined the device is substantially equivalent (for the indications for use stated in the enclosure)

results.finding: Among 670 positive blood cultures, the assay returned susceptibility reports in under 2 hours.
results.detail: Timing began after blood cultures became positive; organisms were identified separately. The assay used 1 mL of culture, excluded polymicrobial samples, and was tested in laboratories and university hospitals. Price and κ reproducibility were not reported.
results.quote: A proprietary software (bioFAST) was used to immediately generate a susceptibility report in less than 2 h.

results.finding: In 278 women with suspected uncomplicated UTI, the near-patient PA-100 returned susceptibility results within 45 min.
results.detail: The 400 µL urine input met the volume target, but the device did not report pathogen species. Hands-on time, inter-user/site reproducibility, price and district or sub-district hospital deployment were not reported. Patients with complicated UTI were excluded.
results.quote: The analyser delivered bacteriuria results in 15 min and AST results within 45 min.

results.finding: QolorPhAST identified bacteria and profiled susceptibility in a suspected-UTI cohort of unspecified size in 36 minutes.
results.detail: The text reports 50 urine specimens for a no-antibiotic growth condition but does not specify the size of the identification and susceptibility cohort. It does not establish district-hospital deployment or the required input volume, hands-on time, inter-user/site reproducibility and individual-test prices.
results.quote: In a proof-of-concept clinical study, QolorPhAST was tested with a cohort of blinded patient samples suspected of urinary tract infections, achieving 100% accuracy in species identification, an average categorical agreement of 91.81% and an average essential agreement of 86.4%, with a turnaround time of 36 min from specimen introduction to result.
